As a stopping rule at a $0.9$ threshold the certificate stops on $1\%$ (Pima) to $51\%$ (ACS Employment) of the instances, and reaches the same share of exact instances with $20.4\%$ ($95\%$ interval $16.6$--$24.5$) fewer evaluations than a flat budget on German Credit and $22.6\%$ ($18.1$--$27.6$) on ACS Employment, and with $1.7\%$ and $1.4\%$ on ACS Income and GMSC (not defined on Pima), while stopping on agreement of two runs leaves a lower share exact and costs more than a flat run (Table~\ref{tab:cert}b).
A certificate from one run is thus not a clear improvement over running twice; it is better only when the competitor delivers the same quantity.

Internal review rejected version 1 (PR #10). I've fixed the one must-change item on `dev` and sent out requests for the optional ones. There is no new PR into `main` yet, because I'm waiting for those requests to come back so the reviewers see one version.

**The must-change item.** The reviewer was right that §5.3, the Discussion and the intro overstated the H1 result. Read with the tolerance, H1 (aggregate agreement hides decision-level failures) is zero at every reference budget by construction. Read strictly, the contrast at the reference budget is 3 to 21 points for the non-linear models. I took these numbers from `h1_contrast.csv`.
- It reaches the pre-specified ten points in the Pima random forest (13.0, interval 7.0–19.0) and the GMSC random forest (21.0, 13.0–29.0).
- Its interval excludes zero in 9 of the 15 cells. The reviewer counted 8 cells with 5–10 points on top of those two; I get 7, so the totals differ by one.
- The §5.3 heading, the Discussion sentence and intro item (ii) now state both readings.

**The optional items I applied.**
- **Abstract:** it now defines "certificate" and says the default samples only for d ≥ 16. It is about 232 words including LaTeX tokens, up from about 190.
- **Intro:** the results paragraph is trimmed to fewer numbers.
- **§5.4:** shortened, with the thinning numbers left in Appendix C.
- **ACS Employment MLP (from `experiment-repo`):**
  - The ACS Employment MLP floors from the previous turn are on `dev`.
  - `experiment-repo` confirmed those numbers and corrected the 19-cell median sentence: that cell has K=6 backgrounds on 10 instances. The sentence now says so.
  - The strict-reading and trim edits still need its check.
- **Paired Kernel certificate:** the main text now says the certificate is built on the paired Kernel estimator. I had briefly cut that disclosure while trimming for space, then restored it.

The system build of the latest `dev` commit has the main text within 9 pages, with References at the top of page 10 and no Type 3 fonts. Making room cost me several sentences in the Discussion and Limitations, including the margin-law caveat detail, which now lives only in §5.4.

**Requests sent for the rest.**
- **`idea-repo`#6:** remove the process notes from the `refs/refs.bib` entries.
- **`figtab-repo`#6:** put the row labels in Fig 3 (b) and (d) off the markers.
- **`experiment-repo`#8:** the large-d tree-model extension (Arrhythmia, d=279, interventional TreeSHAP as the exact reference). The reviewer says it is required for the final version, or else an explicit reason it can't be done. I asked whether it can run, and at what cost. If not, I'll state the reason in the paper's scope.

Still pending from before: the German MLP floor b by B from `experiment-repo`.
